title: Foundations: Hardcore Punk - The Complete Guide
summary: What Hardcore Punk is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Hardcore Punk songs: Hardcore punk is punk stripped to fury: 90-second songs, breakdowns, and shouted ethics about straight edge, unity, and resistance. Minor Threat's 1981 output defined it in 13 songs.

History: Black Flag, Minor Threat, Bad Brains, and SSD built the early-80s hardcore scene: all-ages shows, $5 doors, and a network of fanzines and indie labels (Dischord).

How the songs work: Hardcore Punk favors the keys of E, D, C. Common forms include Verse-chorus in under two minutes; Breakdown: half-time slam section. Players should master the breakdown: everyone jumps in half time first, then stage dives timed to the chorus. Detuned aggression; no capos.

title: Hardcore Punk Etude No. 1: Breakdown i–VII–VI
summary: An original Hardcore Punk study in D drilling stage dives timed to the chorus.
body:
This original etude isolates the 'Breakdown i–VII–VI' progression in the key of D — the changes Hardcore Punk players must know cold.

CHART:
Dm | C | A# | A

FORM: breakdown: half-time slam section.

PRACTICE: loop the chart slowly, adding stage dives timed to the chorus once the changes are clean. Then transpose with the included program and drill it in all twelve keys — the Hardcore Punk player's rite of passage.

title: Straight Edge - Hardcore Punk Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Straight Edge by Minor Threat (1981).
body:
Straight Edge — Minor Threat, 1981. 46 seconds that named a movement.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of C):
C5 | F5 | G5 | C5

This study chart uses the 'Speed I–IV–V' progression, the Hardcore Punk workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus in under two minutes. Listen for shouted vocals, no singing — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Hardcore Punk pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let shouted vocals, no singing. Detuned aggression; no capos. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
